The Hills of California is hugely enjoyable, achingly poignant and brimful of humour spiced with brassy northern wit.
Set over three hours it's a painful and funny well-observed portrait of stymied female ambition, disappointment, and frayed mother-daughter bonds.

cn.t: Butterworth's female-centered family drama earns widespread praise for its rich writing, stellar ensemble led by Laura Donnelly, and Sam Mendes' direction, though some critics find it overlong and less disciplined than his masterpiece Jerusalem.
